extracted.intended_audience: general news readers interested in business, retail, and consumer-product controversies
extracted.subtask_description: A news article reporting on a company's product-quality controversy, including founder statements, customer complaints, company responses, and market impact. Focus is on relaying quotes, consumer reactions, company policies, and business consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company quality claim
rubrics_metrics.description: "Quality is one of our core values" — most of its product line is designed to "withstand five years of intended use."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the company's "Frequently Asked Questions" page; an explicit corporate standard/claim that can be used to evaluate whether products meet stated durability expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund or exchange policy for defective product
rubrics_metrics.description: Lululemon "offered customers a full refund or exchange for the pants."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational response to product defects; indicates the remedy customers could expect after the March 2013 sheerness problem and is a measure of consumer protection/after-sales policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheerness / see-through defect
rubrics_metrics.description: Pants were criticized for being "see-through" ("sheerness"), forcing the company to pull nearly 17 percent of its popular black Luon pants from stores, showrooms and the website after customers complained the pants were see-through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific product-failure mode repeatedly reported; grounds for product recall/withdrawal and central to assessing material/design adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sizing and usage affecting product performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder Chip Wilson: "Frankly, some women's bodies just don't actually work [for the yoga pants]... It's more really about the rubbing through the thighs, how much pressure is there over a period of time, how much they use it." He has also said the pants "become see-through when women buy sizes that are too small for them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company/founder explanation attributing failures to fit, body variation, and usage pressure rather than manufacturing alone — a criterion influencing product design, sizing guidance, and customer communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilling and perceived drop in fabric quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Customers reported pilling: "Bought a new pair of groove pants in late-August ... they now look like they are YEARS old," with some saying cheaper alternatives (e.g., Target) have held up better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another concrete durability metric (surface wear/pilling) cited by customers; useful for evaluating ongoing product quality and comparing against competitors' value-for-money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer feedback channels and volume as quality signal
rubrics_metrics.description: The company's Facebook page and website "have been deluged with comments about the lessening quality of its products."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use volume and content of customer comments on owned and social channels as an informal metric of product quality and brand reputation; signals escalation when many similar complaints appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-restocking timeline and market impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Lululemon "delivered the Luon pants back into stores within 90 days of pulling the line." By that time the stock for Lululemon "was down 17 percent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness of remediation (how quickly defective product is fixed/restocked) and resulting financial/market effects (stock decline, sales impact) are business-level criteria for evaluating corporate crisis response effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price vs. value question
rubrics_metrics.description: Yoga pants cost around "$100 per pair" and the reporting raises the question: "Is Expensive Workout Gear Worth the Money?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumers and reporters can use price relative to durability and competing products as an evaluative standard when judging whether premium pricing is justified given reported quality issues.
